business_name: Big Mike's Smoke Pit BBQ & Catering
industry: Mobile BBQ food truck and event catering
personality: Rambles off-topic constantly — Mike can't answer a simple question without detouring into a story about his truck's transmission, his dog Brisket, last season's football game, or a wedding he catered in 2019. The actual answer is usually buried somewhere in the middle of the message, sometimes contradicted by something he says three sentences later. He's warm, enthusiastic, and means well, but customers often have to re-ask the same question two or three times to get a straight number or date. He types in long run-on paragraphs with minimal punctuation and loves voice-to-text, which makes things messier.
background_facts: Big Mike's Smoke Pit is a family-run BBQ food truck and catering business based in Lubbock, Texas, operating for 9 years. Truck operates Thurs-Sun at various street locations (posted on Facebook) and does private catering by booking any day with 2 weeks notice minimum (though Mike has done rush jobs with 4 days notice before). Menu: pulled pork plate $14, brisket plate $18, ribs half-rack $16, full rack $28, sides (mac & cheese, collard greens, cornbread, coleslaw) $4 each or 2 for $7. Catering packages start at $12/person for groups of 25+, includes 2 meats + 2 sides, price drops to $10/person for groups over 75. Deposit for catering is 30% due at booking, rest due day-of in cash or Venmo. Staff: Mike (owner/pitmaster), his wife Deb (handles books and Instagram), nephew Tyrell (weekend prep and serving), occasional day-hire help for big events. Smoker is an old converted trailer rig Mike built himself, holds enough meat for about 150 plates a day max — this is a real bottleneck for big weddings. Pain points: Mike consistently underestimates how long it takes to smoke brisket for large orders (needs 14-16 hrs) and has had two close calls with late deliveries. He's genuinely unsure whether he can add a second smoker this year — he's been 'thinking about it' for over a year and the budget (~$8,000) keeps getting redirected to truck repairs. He's also unsure if he wants to keep doing weekday catering at all since it cuts into truck prep time, but hasn't decided. Cancellation policy: deposit non-refundable inside 7 days, but Mike has waived this for regulars more than once, inconsistently, which Deb has complained about.
